title: Some scaffolds end at a grade boundary
statement: Remove a scaffold outright at a grade boundary, rather than fading it, when the skill it supports is expected as a matter of course from then on.
example: One course makes quote insertion a grade 4 expectation rather than a supported step.
detail: Guidance on what changes from grade 3 to grade 4 lists seven deliberate departures, one of them that some scaffolds are removed outright, not faded, such as help putting quotes in, because children are expected to do it as a matter of course. So quote insertion becomes a grade 4 expectation, not a supported step, and sentence starters are named as something to reduce. Lesson research for a grade 4 evidence lesson draws the consequence that starters of the 'According to the text' kind are the wrong direction: the quote goes in because the child puts it in.
against: Nothing is built yet: the repo's own table reads "| Remove quote scaffolds | Not applicable yet, no quote scaffold built | Do not build one for Grade 4 |" (`grade3-reading/course-renderer/docs/pedagogy/grade-4-vs-grade-3.md`, line 80).

evidence.quote: **6. Some scaffolds are removed outright, not faded.** "We will want to absolutely remove scaffolding around like putting quotes in and stuff like that, which is things that we want them to be doing just as a matter of course." So quote insertion is a Grade 4 expectation, not a supported step.
So sentence starters of the "According to the text" family, which dominate the practitioner material found, are the wrong direction for us. The quote goes in because the child puts it in.
Sentence starters are named in the same breath as something to reduce.
